chapter: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
title: Checking Feather: Blue Devils, Moten, Little Rock, and never a trio
summary: Basie says he does not recall the year with Page's Blue Devils, never worked with Elmer Payne, went to Little Rock after leaving Moten, and never led a trio.

bands.name: Elmer Payne and His Ten Royal Americans

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: It says, "Deputized in Walter Page's Blue Devils in Dallas, July, '28, 1928," is that right?
I don't remember. I don't remember the year.
And shortly -- so you teamed up with Walter Page in Dallas and you were on the road with somebody else?
Yes, you already know that. You already told me that, way up there, I think.
You were on the road with Kate -- Katy?
: Okay. "And shortly afterwards, joined the band. Left Walter Page in 1929."
: "Briefly with Elmer Payne (PHONETIC) and His Ten Royal Americans?"
Oh, Lord. Well, where would this be then?
I don't know. I don't know where they get Elmer at, but I know him very well. He had a band in there, but I never was in his band.
: "Then joined Bennie Moten's band. Left Moten early in '34 to lead own band under Moten's auspices in Little Rock, Arkansas."
Left Moten (inaudible). I left Benny's band, then we went to Little Rock. But under (inaudible) Benny's?
: You left -- all right. You left Moten. You went to Little Rock with your own band.

I don't know. "Rejoined Benny Moten after that leader's death in 1935, continued to work for a short time under Buster Moten's leadership." Okay. "Returned to Kansas City, worked as a single." After leaving Buster, you worked as a single?
You never did that in Kansas City then? Then with your own trio?
Never did it with your own trio?
Before jointly leading Barons of Rhythm with altoist Buster Smith?
Yeah, that was before the trios, before.
I have never had a trio.
